today.label: Trains: typed pipelines of small steps
State machines shared by the browser and the server
A CLI that reads OpenAPI or GraphQL

milestones.title: Composition
milestones.outcome: Trains run branches in parallel, state machine states start trains, and a failed run resumes from a checkpoint instead of starting over.
points: Parallel branches inside one run, recorded per branch
A machine state that invokes a train and moves on when it finishes or fails
Checkpoints, and resuming a run from a chosen step
All of it visible in GraphQL and the dashboard

code.caption: Sketch, not final
code.text:
Chain<LoadCorpus>()
    .Parallel(p => p
        .Branch(b => b.Chain<EmbeddingSimilarity>())
        .Branch(b => b.Chain<CoCitationOverlap>()))
    .Chain<CombineSignals>()
    .Resolve();

m.In(Partition.Ingesting)
    .Invokes<IIngestPartitionTrain>(ctx => new IngestInput(ctx.Source))
    .OnDone(Partition.Ingested)
    .OnFailed(Partition.Failed);

milestones.title: Machines become the API
milestones.outcome: Each state machine is served as its own typed API. The server applies every transition, and pushes each new snapshot to the client over the socket.
points: One typed mutation per event, generated from the machine
Authorization per event, checked on the server
Every operation persisted, so production can refuse ad-hoc queries
Snapshot changes pushed over a subscription, including ones the server made itself

milestones.title: Generated clients
milestones.outcome: The CLI generates the whole client side for a frontend framework: the machines, a typed function per operation, and live progress. Your frontend code is the views.
points: React first, on a framework-neutral core
Calls send persisted operation hashes, never query text
Typed progress for trains as they run

milestones.title: From a spec to a running app
milestones.outcome: Give the CLI an OpenAPI or GraphQL spec, choose your security and which schemas become tables, and get an API that runs, not one full of stubs.
points: Auth from the shipped packages (API key, JWT, Cognito, OIDC), closed by default
Postgres or SQLite tables with migrations, from the spec's schemas
Working create, read, update and delete operations
Re-running after the spec changes keeps the code you wrote

milestones.title: One app, end to end
milestones.outcome: A complete sample app built only with the CLI, and a guide that takes you from a spec to the same result.
points: A full working app, not a feature demo
A guide checked to work from top to bottom
